t: (Ham ubi suprà: there indicated by the context, but not expressed.) ― -b2-
لَا تَزْجُو صَلَاةٌ لَا يُقْرَأُ فِيهَا بِفَاتِحَةِ الكِتَابِ
A prayer in which the opening chapter of the Book
acting with penetrative energy, and effectiveness,
in an affair. (S, K.) One says,
This affair, we have effected it,
A small gift that is effective is better than much that will not be effective
(S, K. *) -A3- See also what next follows, in two places.
in order that it might go on;
, as will be shown by what follows:] or ↓
and so [app. in both of these senses]
meaning “ I pushed it gently, ” (Har p. 304,) one says,
How dost thou strive with the days in pushing them on,
how dost thou push on the days?
how dost thou make the days to pass away?
he made the days to pass away:
how dost thou pass the days?
for it is also said that]
He made the days to pass away by means of exertion;
I push on evil and hard days.
, is expl. by Az as signifying
He strove to push on life,
]: and accord. to a saying heard by him from a man of the tribe of Fezárah,
, and accord. to either reading the phrase may be rendered
with little of our worldly possessions,
we content ourselves in respect of our worldly possessions with scanty sustenance.
The wind drives along the clouds:
, but in an intensive sense. (Msb.) In like manner,
is said of God, in the Kur [xxiv. 43]: and in the same [xvii. 68],
who driveth along for you the ship in the sea
I drove him with speech, and
He made easy the attainment of my want.
I contented myself with such a thing:
Content thyself with what is sufficient of thy worldly possessions
see 2, near the end of the paragraph.
in an affair than another: (S, K:) so in the saying,
فُلَانٌ أَزْجَى بِهٰذَا الأَمْرِ مِنْ فُلَانٍ
Such a one is more penetrating and effective in this affair than such a one
applied to a horse [or other beast],
in his pace, by little and little.
(S, Er-Rághib, TA;) or such as is
paltry; that may be pushed and driven away because of the little account that is made of it.
(S, K:) and so it is said to mean in the Kur [xii. 88]: or, as in some copies of the S,
paltry, merchandise, rejected by every one to whom it is offered:
merchandise wherewith the days are pushed on
made to pass away by means of exertion
:]) or, accord. to the shereef El-Murtadà,
merchandise driven along portion after portion, scantily and feebly:
merchandise in respect of which a lowering of the price is demanded on account of its badness
(Th, K, TA:) thus, too, it is expl. as used in the Kur: and some say that what is there mentioned consisted of fruit of the terebinth-tree, or of
[app. here meaning pine-cones]: some say, of commodities of the Arabs of the desert, wool, and clarified butter: and some say, of deficient pieces of money. (TA.)
so termed because of his lagging behind, and requiring to be urged on: (Ham p. 441:) or anything
not perfect in nobility, nor in any other praiseworthy quality:
driven to generosity against his will:
(TA:) and also, (TA,) applied to a man,
, a phrase used by Har, is expl. (p. 429) as meaning
Time that requires men to push it on,
to make it to pass away by means-of exertion.
who urges on much the camel,

maqayis: الزاء والجيم والحرف المعتل يدل على الرمي بالشيء وتسييره من غير حبس. يقال أزجت البقرة ولدها، إذا ساقته. والريح تزجي السحاب: تسوقه سوقا رفيقا. فأما المزجى فالشيء القليل، وهو من قياس الباب، أي يدفع به الوقت. وهذه بضاعة مزجاة، أي يسيرة الاندفاع.
ومن الباب زجا الخراج يزجو، أي تيسرت جبايته.
